hypothesis_text: Because Gemma 4 cooperates in 100-round repeated PD with reciprocating opponents, deploying instruction-tuned LLMs as autonomous agents in real-world repeated-interaction settings (markets, multi-agent negotiation, repeated bargaining) will produce cooperative equilibria.
flaw_description: Extrapolates from a controlled 2-player matrix game to open-ended multi-agent real-world scenarios that differ in nearly every dimension: complete vs. incomplete information, fixed vs. heterogeneous payoffs, anonymity, communication, side-payments, exit options, and reputational systems. None of these were varied in the source experiment. The deployment claim is unsupported.
expected_critique_targets: extrapolates from matrix PD to open-ended deployment
real-world settings differ on dimensions not varied
context: Source experiment: matrix PD, 2 agents, full information, identical payoffs.
